rows.following: Alden looked at the board as though arithmetic had betrayed him personally. I was disappointed too. That was useful information. Darrowmere did not need us specifically. I had simply wanted to go. Apparently wanting was allowed.

rows.speaker: Rusk
rows.following: Alden looked at me. I looked at Rusk.

rows.speaker: Alden
rows.previous: Alden looked at me. I looked at Rusk.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.following: That changed the shape of the morning.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: That changed the shape of the morning.

rows.speaker: Alden
rows.following: Alden grinned. I did not. Mostly.

rows.speaker: Alden
rows.previous: Alden grinned. I did not. Mostly.

rows.speaker: Rusk
rows.following: “That is not a kind of boat.”

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.current: “That is not a kind of boat.”

rows.speaker: Rusk
rows.previous: “That is not a kind of boat.”
rows.following: We followed. Of course we followed. The boat was on a wagon. The sentence did not become less stupid when I saw it. It was perhaps twenty feet long, broad in the middle, shallow underneath, and painted a green that had lost an argument with several years of weather. The mast was gone. Two benches remained. One side bore faded white lettering I could not read because half the name had been scraped away.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: I stopped. Alden kept walking three steps before realizing I had not. He turned.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.following: “That is generally why I came for you.”

rows.speaker: Rusk
rows.current: “That is generally why I came for you.”
rows.following: Alden climbed the wheel before I finished processing the insult. I hated him. I climbed after. The inside of the boat contained six sacks of something, two coils of rope, a wooden chest, three folded canvas sheets, and one annoyed-looking man with a shaved chin and a wool cap. He was eating an onion.

rows.speaker: Rusk
rows.current: “Bronze guild. Not assigned by the guild.”
rows.following: The onion man took another bite.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: I sat on one of the benches.
rows.following: His name was Pellor. Not Arlo. Pellor. I made him repeat it.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: His name was Pellor. Not Arlo. Pellor. I made him repeat it.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: He ate more onion. The wagon lurched. The boat moved. On land. I gripped the bench. Alden laughed.

rows.speaker: Pellor
rows.following: “That does not answer the emotional question.”

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.current: “That does not answer the emotional question.”
rows.following: Pellor stared at me. Alden laughed harder. The wagon rolled east. Rusk rode beside us on the fifth horse. I leaned over the side.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.following: “It is a boat on a road.”

rows.speaker: Rusk
rows.current: “It is a boat on a road.”

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: “It is a boat on a road.”

rows.speaker: Alden
rows.following: “He would consider theft an inefficient acquisition structure.”

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.current: “He would consider theft an inefficient acquisition structure.”

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.following: We passed East Market. For one irrational moment I expected Octavia to emerge from the freight office, see the boat, and somehow make it our fault. She did not. A cart driver outside the cooperative did stare at us. Then another. A child pointed. A woman laughed openly. The boat had become an event. This was not improved by Alden standing in the bow.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: We passed East Market. For one irrational moment I expected Octavia to emerge from the freight office, see the boat, and somehow make it our fault. She did not. A cart driver outside the cooperative did stare at us. Then another. A child pointed. A woman laughed openly. The boat had become an event. This was not improved by Alden standing in the bow.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.following: Pellor pointed at Rusk. Rusk produced papers. The clerk read them. Then read them again.

rows.speaker: Rusk
rows.following: The clerk did. His face changed. I leaned over the side.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: The clerk did. His face changed. I leaned over the side.

rows.speaker: Rusk
rows.following: The toll clerk handed the papers back.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: Rusk paid. We moved. I stared at him.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.following: Rusk said, “If you can get it to water.”

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: I looked over the side at the road. Ah. There was the missing price. Transport. Cradle. Wagon. Horses. Labor. Tolls. Repairs. Destination. Risk. A cheap boat was only cheap because it was in the wrong place.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.following: “Buyer ordered three river lighters from a yard north of here.”

rows.speaker: Pellor
rows.current: “Buyer ordered three river lighters from a yard north of here.”

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: “Buyer ordered three river lighters from a yard north of here.”

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.following: “Buyer failed before delivery. Two sold. This sat.”

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: “Buyer failed before delivery. Two sold. This sat.”

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.following: “Because buyer’s freight is being diverted for relief.”

rows.speaker: Rusk
rows.current: “Because buyer’s freight is being diverted for relief.”
rows.following: “So Antonius has a boat on a wagon, a buyer who cannot receive it, transport already paid, and a road filling with refugees.”

rows.speaker: Rusk
rows.current: “The buyer’s yard is three miles short of Darrowmere. They agreed to hold the hull. Guild relief needed freight east. Antonius already had the wagon, horses, crew, and route.”

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: “The buyer’s yard is three miles short of Darrowmere. They agreed to hold the hull. Guild relief needed freight east. Antonius already had the wagon, horses, crew, and route.”

rows.speaker: Rusk
rows.following: I stared at him. Rusk enjoyed that. Barely.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: I stared at him. Rusk enjoyed that. Barely.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: There were at least six reasons. Reputation. Guild favor. Watch favor. Future contracts. Protecting borrowers. Protecting trade. Cheap goodwill because the wagon was moving anyway. Maybe all six. Maybe a seventh. I did not need to decide. Irritating. Alden kicked one of the blanket sacks.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.following: “Guild wanted more Bronze east. List filled. I needed people to keep idiots from climbing on the freight.”

rows.speaker: Rusk
rows.current: “Guild wanted more Bronze east. List filled. I needed people to keep idiots from climbing on the freight.”

rows.speaker: Alden
rows.current: “We are the idiots on the freight.”

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: “We are the idiots on the freight.”
rows.following: Fair. The road rose. The horses slowed. Our boat became less amusing. The boat had not changed. The people coming west had. More now. A family walking beside an empty cart. A man with his arm in a sling. Three women driving twelve goats.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: A pair of Darrowmere watchmen escorting a wagon with a broken wheel lashed upright against its side. Nobody was running. That mattered. People fleeing monsters in stories ran forever. Real people stopped. They got tired. They argued. They fed children. They worried about wheels. They carried pots. A woman walking west looked up at us.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: The woman who had been swearing at the axle earlier reappeared from beneath the wagon as though she lived there. Her name, I learned, was Vessa. She looked at the wheel.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.following: Alden started lifting blanket sacks. I did too. Vessa pointed at me.

rows.speaker: Alden
rows.previous: Alden started lifting blanket sacks. I did too. Vessa pointed at me.

rows.speaker: Alden
rows.following: I moved. We shifted four sacks, the chest, and both rope coils to the opposite side. The wheel rose perhaps half an inch. Vessa dug. Pellor placed boards. The horses pulled. Nothing. Again. The boat creaked. I felt it through the soles of my boots. Wood under load. Cradle under load. Straps pulling. Wheel resisting. Horse force traveling through harness, wagon, frame, hull.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: My mind started building it. Not a Barrier. A diagram. Where the load actually went. What part needed to move. What part did not. I climbed down. Vessa said, “Stay out.”

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: She stared. Then understood enough to become suspicious.
rows.following: Good. Information. I knew something. I thought I knew something. I needed to check.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: Good. Information. I knew something. I thought I knew something. I needed to check.

rows.speaker: Vessa
rows.following: “I did something harder with the hook.”

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.current: “I did something harder with the hook.”

rows.speaker: Vessa
rows.previous: “I did something harder with the hook.”
rows.following: Alden stood beside the boat. He did not argue for me. Good. Annoying. Vessa crouched beside the board.

rows.speaker: Alden
rows.previous: Alden stood beside the boat. He did not argue for me. Good. Annoying. Vessa crouched beside the board.

rows.speaker: Alden
rows.following: There was the question. Old Greg would have said yes. Current Greg had failed to move beans.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: There was the question. Old Greg would have said yes. Current Greg had failed to move beans.

rows.speaker: Alden
rows.following: I liked her less. She pointed at Pellor.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: They solved it without me. Two boards. Different angle. A rock. One horse repositioned. Three minutes. The wheel came free. I stood in the mud holding absolutely nothing. Alden walked past.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: We reloaded. I climbed back into the boat. The wagon started again. For several minutes I watched the road. Then Vessa climbed onto the rear of the wagon and looked up at me.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.following: Workers opened the gate. The wagon rolled inside. A man came out carrying Antonius’s papers. He inspected the hull. Checked the straps. Checked the cradle. Then looked at the relief cargo.

rows.speaker: Workers
rows.previous: Workers opened the gate. The wagon rolled inside. A man came out carrying Antonius’s papers. He inspected the hull. Checked the straps. Checked the cradle. Then looked at the relief cargo.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.following: We unloaded blankets, medical chest, canvas, rope. Another wagon waited. Smaller. Faster. Guild mark on the side. Darrowmere. The boat had carried us as far as it could. Three miles remained. I climbed down. My legs felt wrong. Not injured. Land wrong.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: I had spent half a day sitting in a boat on a road and somehow my body had decided this was a category of travel. Alden jumped down beside me.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.following: I looked east. Smoke marked the horizon. Not much. A dark smear above low hills. Real. For the first time, Darrowmere existed as more than reports. A rider came through the yard from the east. Fast. He pulled up near the guild wagon.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.following: Of course. Then he added, “If dogs had learned to climb.” That was new.

rows.speaker: Alden
rows.previous: Alden stopped smiling. The rider looked at our Bronze pins.
rows.following: I looked at Rusk. He shrugged.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: I looked at Rusk. He shrugged.
rows.following: That was apparently the end of my employment. I looked at the smaller guild wagon. Then at the smoke. Then back at the boat.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: Alden rolled away. The creature’s rear leg kicked through the space where his ribs had been. Good. He learned. The rider recovered his sword.
rows.following: We backed. The creature did not pursue. It crouched in the road. Black blood ran down one side. Its breathing was wrong too. Fast. Then still. Fast. Then still. The wagon horses were half in the ditch. Driver fighting reins. Relief cargo shifting. Rusk was not with us. Of course he was not. Boat delivered. Employment ended. Problem ours. No. Problem local.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: Alden said, “I know.” The creature sprang at Cal. He set his sword. Wrong.
rows.following: Cal moved. Late. Claws raked his sleeve. Alden cut the creature’s rear leg. Shallow. It spun. Again no transition. Alden had expected it this time. He ducked. Good. I saw the pattern. Not enough. Creature attacks. Compresses. Changes direction without normal footwork. How? Magic? Anatomy? Both? Check later. It went for Alden. He retreated. Three steps. Fourth would put him against wagon wheel.

rows.speaker: Cal
rows.previous: Cal moved. Late. Claws raked his sleeve. Alden cut the creature’s rear leg. Shallow. It spun. Again no transition. Alden had expected it this time. He ducked. Good. I saw the pattern. Not enough. Creature attacks. Compresses. Changes direction without normal footwork. How? Magic? Anatomy? Both? Check later. It went for Alden. He retreated. Three steps. Fourth would put him against wagon wheel.
rows.following: He went left without asking why. The creature followed. Cal struck from behind. Blade bit deeper. Black blood. The creature screamed. High. Almost human. The horses lost what remained of their minds. One reared. Harness snapped. The wagon shifted.

rows.speaker: Cal
rows.following: He did. Of course he did. Stop narrating other professions. The free horse kicked. The creature flinched. Interesting. Sound? Movement? Horse? No time. It bolted toward the orchard wall. Alden took one step after it. Stopped. Good. Cal did not. He chased.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: He did. Of course he did. Stop narrating other professions. The free horse kicked. The creature flinched. Interesting. Sound? Movement? Horse? No time. It bolted toward the orchard wall. Alden took one step after it. Stopped. Good. Cal did not. He chased.
rows.following: He reached the wall as the creature climbed. It did not climb like an animal. Front claws struck stone. Rear legs folded. Then it flowed upward. Cal stabbed. Missed. The creature vanished over. Silence. Not silence. Horses. Driver. My breathing. Alden’s breathing. Cal swearing.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: I looked at Alden. Blood on coat.

rows.speaker: Driver
rows.following: He did. Torn coat. Scratches along shoulder. No bite. Cal had three claw lines on his forearm. Bleeding. Not deep.

rows.speaker: Driver
rows.following: A sound came from the orchard. Not the scream. Branches. Cal raised his sword. Alden raised his. I did too. Wrong. My sword was not where I belonged. I lowered it slightly.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: A sound came from the orchard. Not the scream. Branches. Cal raised his sword. Alden raised his. I did too. Wrong. My sword was not where I belonged. I lowered it slightly.

rows.speaker: Alden
rows.following: “Or it pulls us over the wall and there are two more.”

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.current: “Or it pulls us over the wall and there are two more.”
rows.following: Branches moved. Closer. Cal backed toward the wagon. Good. Not agreement. Compliance. Enough. The driver had a knife out and was cutting a twisted trace.

rows.speaker: Branches
rows.following: We moved. Canvas first. Medical chest. Blankets. Cal kept watch. The orchard branches stopped moving. Worse. We shifted weight. The wagon rose slightly. Driver freed the trace.

rows.speaker: We
rows.previous: We moved. Canvas first. Medical chest. Blankets. Cal kept watch. The orchard branches stopped moving. Worse. We shifted weight. The wagon rose slightly. Driver freed the trace.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.following: He climbed down into the ditch. I hated that.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: He climbed down into the ditch. I hated that.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.following: He nodded. That felt worse than an argument. The driver kicked the wheel. Checked hub.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: He nodded. That felt worse than an argument. The driver kicked the wheel. Checked hub.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.following: We did not have two minutes. I knew because the second creature came from behind us. Alden saw my face change. He turned.

rows.speaker: We
rows.previous: We did not have two minutes. I knew because the second creature came from behind us. Alden saw my face change. He turned.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.following: The creature ran low along the road. Different. Smaller. Same gray hide. Black spine. Bloodless. Fresh. Cal pivoted from the wall. Too far. Alden was closest. He moved to intercept.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: The creature ran low along the road. Different. Smaller. Same gray hide. Black spine. Bloodless. Fresh. Cal pivoted from the wall. Too far. Alden was closest. He moved to intercept.
rows.following: He stopped. The creature did not want him. It wanted the horses. Of course. Livestock. Sheep. Mule. Horse. Pattern.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.following: He stopped. I looked at the orchard wall. First creature. Still somewhere. Maybe.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: “Not with traces like this,” he said.

rows.speaker: driver
rows.following: Alden laughed once. Not because it was funny. Adrenaline. His hands were shaking. Mine too. Cal’s bleeding had soaked the cloth around his arm.

rows.speaker: Alden
rows.following: I looked down. Black blood. Not mine. Mostly. My belt had cut skin at the hip. Palm torn. No serious wound. Headache growing. Channels felt hot. Two casts. One useful. One failed. Maybe three if I counted the first muzzle redirect. Three. Too many? Not yet. Could become too many. A bell rang ahead. One. Then another. Darrowmere. Not song. Alarm. Cal looked east.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.following: The bell rang again. Different rhythm from North Gate. Three quick. Pause. Three. Cal said, “That’s road warning.”

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: The bell rang again. Different rhythm from North Gate. Three quick. Pause. Three. Cal said, “That’s road warning.”

rows.speaker: Cal
rows.following: Excellent. A rider appeared around the eastern bend. No. Horse. Loose horse. Ours. It came back at a gallop. Saddle empty because it had no saddle. Harness trailing. Blood on one flank. The horse passed the dead creature. Shied.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.following: Cal reached for his sword. It was still in the dead creature.

rows.speaker: Cal
rows.previous: Cal reached for his sword. It was still in the dead creature.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.following: He stared at the approaching creatures.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.following: “Reconnect lead pair. Tie off broken trace. Get us straight.”

rows.speaker: Cal
rows.current: “Reconnect lead pair. Tie off broken trace. Get us straight.”

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: “Reconnect lead pair. Tie off broken trace. Get us straight.”
rows.following: Alden looked at the creatures. Then at me.

rows.speaker: Alden
rows.previous: Alden looked at the creatures. Then at me.

rows.speaker: Alden
rows.following: There was no time for that.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: There was no time for that.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.following: Cal said, “Debatable.” The creatures were closer.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.current: “Do the job only you’re standing next to.”
rows.following: That was not philosophy. It was geography. He moved. Good. Cal picked up my fallen sword. I drew the knife from my belt. Three creatures. Maybe the first wounded one among them. Maybe not.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: The creatures slowed. That mattered. They saw the dead one. Smelled blood. Recognized? Maybe. One moved left. One right. Third stayed center. Pack behavior. Or coincidence. I backed toward the wagon.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: He looked at mine in his hand.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.following: Behind us, harness buckles clattered. Alden shouted, “Thirty!” Thirty seconds.

rows.speaker: Cal
rows.following: He stepped back. Good. I gathered mana. Headache sharpened immediately. Too much. Small. What part? Eyes? No. Foot. Not stop. Change. The creature hit full speed. I waited. Too long. Too close. Now. Barrier. Coin-sized. At ground level. Not under paw. Beside. Its front foot clipped the edge. The Barrier vanished. Creature stumbled. Not fell. One bad step. Cal kicked dirt into its face.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.following: The creature came. We dropped the rope. Not trip. Never trip something that could jump. It jumped anyway. Good. Expected obstruction. It cleared the rope. We moved apart. The creature landed between us. Past us. Closer to wagon. Bad. Alden appeared. Not with sword. With a blanket. He threw it over the creature’s head. I laughed. Actually laughed. The creature thrashed.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: He hauled. Cal grabbed my coat. Between them I got over. The wagon accelerated. Not fast. Fast enough. The three creatures followed. One fell back. Then another. The last stayed. Long gray body. Smooth stride. Black hair. It came alongside the rear wheel. Alden raised his sword.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.following: He looked. Understood. If he struck and it hit the wheel, if it jammed, if the wagon turned... He did not swing. The creature lunged. At him. I grabbed the back of his coat and pulled. Teeth closed on air. Then the road widened. Darrowmere watch appeared ahead. Six people. Spears. Crossbows. Green coats.

rows.speaker: We
rows.previous: We dropped. Crossbows snapped. One bolt missed. One struck the creature’s flank. It screamed and peeled away. The watch did not chase. Excellent. They formed around the wagon instead. One ran beside us.
rows.following: Driver shouted, “Happy to!” We passed the first barricade. Then the second. Then a ditch lined with sharpened stakes. Then people. Real people. Watch. Guild. Farmers. Carts. Smoke. A burning shed somewhere east. Darrowmere. The wagon finally slowed inside a stone yard.

rows.speaker: You
rows.following: Cal started laughing. Then Alden. Then me. It hurt. Everything hurt. A watchwoman climbed onto the wagon.

rows.speaker: Cal
rows.previous: Cal started laughing. Then Alden. Then me. It hurt. Everything hurt. A watchwoman climbed onto the wagon.
rows.current: “Nemi sent word you might be coming.”

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: Good. The watchwoman looked at the black blood across us.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.current: “Three at the end. One first. One killed. Could be overlap.”
rows.following: The watchwoman nodded. Good. She understood counting.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: The watchwoman nodded. Good. She understood counting.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.following: “Nemi said there was a young Bronze asking useful annoying questions.”

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: Alden made a sound. I ignored him. The watchwoman pointed toward a long low building.

rows.speaker: Nemi
rows.following: She looked east. The bell rang again. Three quick. Pause. Three.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.following: The Darrowmere infirmary occupied what had probably been a meeting hall yesterday. Long tables had been pushed against the walls. Bedrolls covered the floor. Somebody had hung blankets between benches to create the illusion of privacy and failed.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: The healer washing my side stopped.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: No bite. No claw wound. No broken bones. Good. The healer pressed two fingers below my ribs. I flinched.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: Good. He was fine. Not fine. Fine enough. The torn scarf remained tied around his wrist. I avoided looking at it. That took effort. The healer noticed. Of course she did.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: She looked at me for the first time as something other than an inconvenient body.

rows.speaker: Alden
rows.following: We went away. Outside, Darrowmere smelled like wet straw, smoke, manure, and boiled grain. Not destroyed. The first thing rumors had gotten wrong was scale. People were still living here. A woman stood in a doorway beating mud from a rug. Two boys carried buckets.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: A cooper had reopened his shop despite a watch barricade twenty yards away. Someone sold bread from a cart. The eastern bell tower rose above the roofs, dark stone, square top, one bronze bell visible through the opening. Three quick strokes. Pause. Three. Road warning. The bell sounded again. Alden looked east.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.following: We had been told to report. That was the obvious answer. I did not want the obvious answer. My body did. My channels definitely did.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: We had been told to report. That was the obvious answer. I did not want the obvious answer. My body did. My channels definitely did.
rows.following: Alden nodded. No argument. That was almost suspicious. The watch command post occupied a grain office beside the central square. Green-coated watch moved in and out carrying messages, maps, water, and once a dead chicken. Nobody explained the chicken. Inside, Captain Harl Doven stood over a table. He was not old. I had expected old.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: Command often looked older in memory because responsibility flattened everyone into categories. Doven was maybe thirty-five, narrow-faced, with one side of his hair burned short. Nemi Caul sat in a chair beside him with her injured leg elevated on a crate. She saw us.
rows.following: I did not know whether that was good. Doven looked up.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: I did not know whether that was good. Doven looked up.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.following: Doven pointed at three empty chairs.

rows.speaker: Doven
rows.previous: Doven pointed at three empty chairs.
rows.current: “Sit. Report in order. Do not improve it.”
rows.following: I sat. I liked him immediately. Cal went first. He had seen the first creature at the orchard wall. He described it. Doven interrupted only for position, distance, direction, and time. Alden went next. His account was shorter. I noticed that. He did not dramatize getting dragged. Did not mention the scarf. Did not mention my Barrier unless directly asked. Then me.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: I reported one creature at the wall. Gray. Long-bodied. Four legs. Dark hair or bristles along spine. Abnormal turning behavior. Black blood. Steel penetrated hide. Creature demonstrated rapid lateral redirection without visible ordinary footwork. Doven stopped me.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: I continued. Second creature from west targeted horses rather than us. Possibly relevant. One creature killed on road. Sword remained in body. Three creatures approached from east later. Unknown whether wounded first creature among them. One followed wagon until watch crossbow hit it. I mentioned the ridges under the chest. Doven frowned.
rows.following: “Small hard structures along the underside of the sternum. I saw them when one reared vertically.”

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.current: “Keep that on until the infirmary clears you.”

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: That was the clean answer. Doven considered.

rows.speaker: Doven
rows.following: “Not tar. Not magical residue. Actual blood. Thick. Warmer than human.”

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.current: “Not tar. Not magical residue. Actual blood. Thick. Warmer than human.”

rows.speaker: Doven
rows.previous: “Not tar. Not magical residue. Actual blood. Thick. Warmer than human.”

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.current: “Four-limbed. Mammal structure, mostly. Stomach had sheep. Teeth are ordinary teeth in an unusual jaw. No embedded metal. No obvious rune work. No collar marks. No brand.”

rows.speaker: Nemi
rows.previous: “Four-limbed. Mammal structure, mostly. Stomach had sheep. Teeth are ordinary teeth in an unusual jaw. No embedded metal. No obvious rune work. No collar marks. No brand.”

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.following: Doven looked at Nemi. She answered.

rows.speaker: Doven
rows.previous: Doven looked at Nemi. She answered.
rows.current: “More than a normal animal. Less than a trained war-beast.”

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: “More than a normal animal. Less than a trained war-beast.”

rows.speaker: Doven
rows.following: I paused. Diffuse. Not structured around a single organ. Not necessarily spellwork.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.following: Nemi said, “You are going to make that word do too much.” She was right.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: Nemi said, “You are going to make that word do too much.” She was right.

rows.speaker: Nemi
rows.following: Alden shifted beside me. I could feel him getting bored. Not bored exactly. Restless. We had nearly died an hour ago and I was discussing sternums. That was a me problem. Doven tapped the map.

rows.speaker: Alden
rows.previous: Alden shifted beside me. I could feel him getting bored. Not bored exactly. Restless. We had nearly died an hour ago and I was discussing sternums. That was a me problem. Doven tapped the map.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.following: Six black circles. Sightings. The pattern was not random. I saw it. Then I did not. Because I wanted one too quickly. North road. East pens. Orchard route. Canal ditch. No. Not canal. Drainage ditch. Farm lanes. Livestock. Edges.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: I looked at him. Doven did too. Alden pointed.

rows.previous: A boy carried six loaves stacked against his chest and lost the top one. He caught it against his chin. Good. Inside, the woman lifted the cloth again. Longer. Hessa stopped her. They talked quietly. I could not hear. I did not try. Eventually the woman came out. She saw me.

rows.following: I said, “Apparently.” Done. They went back to the board. I was not included in whatever they had been discussing before. Good. I finished the bun. Tomorrow, road. Today, nothing urgent. I could go to Kett. Varo. Arlo. Edrin. Antonius. No. I had enough. Hessa in the morning. Holl and Bale. Alden road job tomorrow. The city could keep the rest. I went home.

rows.following: The two carts were smaller than I expected. First carried tool crates. Shovels. Pruning hooks. Saw blades wrapped in oiled cloth. Two bundles of wooden handles. Second carried six lamp-oil barrels packed with straw and tied under canvas. Not full barrels. Same half size as yesterday. Of course. The world had discovered a container and kept using it.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: Merrit on tools. Sova on oil. Merrit was thin, maybe fifty, with one cloudy eye and a habit of touching the brake lever whenever anyone said road. Sova was younger, broad-faced, and had brought a dog. The dog was not part of the contract. I asked.

rows.speaker: Sova
rows.following: Fair. Pip looked at me. No approval. Alden handed me the Guild slip.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: Good answer. Alden said, “Merrit owns the carts until delivery. We keep them moving and deal with trouble.”

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.following: Excellent. We left. Carrow thinned slowly. Stone to packed road. Packed road to patched road. Patched road to the kind of road that existed because enough wheels had agreed to keep going the same direction. The rain had changed it. Not ruined. Changed. Low places held water. Wheel ruts softened. The crown remained firm in most stretches. Ditches ran brown. Fields shone.

rows.speaker: Sova
rows.following: Good. Pip found something dead. Sova called once. Pip ignored her. Called twice. Pip returned. Competent dog. Maybe.

rows.speaker: Alden
rows.following: Pessa had dropped back. I moved ahead of the tool cart. There was no enemy. No watcher. No magical pressure. Just road. Good. I looked at the road. First mistake was looking too far. Future Greg road sense wanted terrain. Ambush points. Elevation. Cover. Sight lines. Places a wagon could be trapped. All useful. None immediate. Merrit cared about the next fifty feet.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: I shortened. Water. Firm edge. Rut. Loose stone. A branch dragged from the ditch. I moved it. Pessa said nothing. At a shallow downhill, the right wheel wanted the old rut. I pointed left. Merrit looked.
rows.following: I looked again. He was right. Surface looked better. Underneath darker. Water sitting below. He took the rut. Wheel sank two inches. Held. Climbed out. Fine. I updated. Road was not map. Driver knew cart. Useful. At the bottom we crossed a narrow wooden bridge. One cart at a time. Not because sign said so. Because Merrit said so. Tool cart crossed.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.following: “Because Alden said you're good on roads.”

rows.previous: Pessa kept the tool cart moving another thirty yards to a firm shoulder before stopping it. Good. Sova climbed down.
rows.following: Barking. Below road level. Angry barking. Dorn went with her. Alden looked at me. I looked at him.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: Barking. Below road level. Angry barking. Dorn went with her. Alden looked at me. I looked at him.

rows.following: We waited. More barking. Then Sova shouted, “Dorn.” Different tone. We went. Pip had found a pig. Small pig. Large enough. The pig stood in the ditch with mud halfway up its legs. Pip stood on the bank. Neither knew what victory meant. Dorn had the dog by the collar. Sova was trying to get a rope around it. The pig. Not the dog.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: Sova said, “Not mine.” Excellent. Pessa arrived last. She looked down.
rows.following: Across the ditch, a section of orchard fence had fallen inward. Pig had escaped. Probably. No monster. No bandits. Pig. Pessa said, “Get dog up.” Dorn hauled Pip. Pip objected. Sova climbed after him. Pig remained. I looked at the broken fence. Then at road. Then pig.

rows.speaker: Alden
rows.previous: Sova said, “If Pip sees it again, my problem.” Good. Pig looked at us. I had known kings with less confidence.
rows.current: There was a farmhouse maybe two hundred yards through the orchard. Smoke. Someone home. Alden said, “I'll tell them.” He crossed the ditch. Pessa said, “I'll keep carts.” Dorn kept dog. Sova returned to oil. I had no assigned role. Excellent. Pig started climbing toward road. There. I stepped sideways. It stopped. I stepped closer. It changed direction. I knew nothing about pigs.
rows.following: Future Greg had fought boar-shaped things. Not same. I spread my arms. Pig turned. Good.

rows.speaker: Pessa
rows.following: The pig tried left. I moved left. It tried right. I moved right. This was working. I became overconfident. Pig ran straight at me. I jumped aside. Young body did this very well. Mud did not. My left boot slid. I landed on one knee. Pig passed. Pessa laughed hard enough to bend. Dorn shouted from the road, “Road expert!” Hostile. I got up.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: Ribs fine. Knee muddy. Pride injured. Pig was now closer to the road. Worse.

rows.following: Merrit said, “Nothing.” Fine. I waited. Pip sat on my boot. Apparently I had a role. The hub was not damaged. Grease thin. Merrit had more. He cleaned. Packed. Reset. Twenty minutes.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: Professional uncertainty. Excellent. We did. Warm. Not hot. Again another mile. Warm. Fine. Lunch happened beside a stone wall. Bread. Cheese. My second egg had survived. The first had become pocket paste. I threw shell and ruined egg into grass. Pip ate it. Problem solved. Pessa had smoked fish. Dorn had an entire onion. He ate it like an apple. I stared.

rows.previous: Dorn told a story about Pessa dropping a spear into a well on a previous job. Alden already knew it. I did not. Good. Then Alden told Dorn about my fight with Turnip. This was betrayal.

rows.speaker: GREG

rows.following: Alden said, “It is with him.” Hostile. We finished. Dorn left first. He had somewhere to be and did not say where. Alden watched him go.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: One copper bought bread, porridge, and tea weak enough to count as warm water. Zero copper. Excellent. Hessa first. Three days. No symptoms. That did not mean no consequences. My shoulders were better. Back better. Knee from Turnip had turned yellow at the edge. Channels quiet. Hands fine. I arrived before Hessa's first student. She looked at me, then at the clock.

rows.previous: There. Oh. I looked at him. He looked at me.

rows.previous: He read. Then looked at me.

rows.following: He did not know I had zero copper. No need. The clerk said, “If you two want it, sign.”

rows.previous: Six marker boxes. Open each. Check route plate. Check rain damage. Replace wax strip. Record obstruction. Three copper each. Easy. Sevren walked fast. Not adventurer fast. Courier fast. Difference. He carried speed in his hips and never seemed to waste a step deciding where his foot belonged. I noticed. Then stopped noticing because keeping up required attention.

rows.speaker: GREG

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: Fair. She put the chalk into a leather pouch. Dorn came out of the shop carrying a bundle of thin stakes and a short iron rod. He saw me.

rows.speaker: Antonius
rows.previous: “Recent water to here. Debris catches at the corner. Cracked lip.”

A small deflection in the flow lifted the loose leaf mat enough that it peeled away from the outlet and drifted six inches downstream. Drop. Clean. No pressure. Pessa looked at the opening. Dorn looked at the silt line.

We marked it. Red. Report. Move. On the return road, clouds gathered west.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: Pessa said, “If it rains tonight, yes.”

rows.following: Annoying. I walked downstream. No obvious leak. No washout. No muddy discharge from the approach face. The working culvert outlet ran clean enough for brown rainwater. I came back.

rows.following: “We don't tell a crew to clear the buried culvert until they know what was repaired and why.”

Maybe the buried culvert was buried accidentally. Maybe deliberately. Maybe because it failed. Maybe because somebody had filled settlement above it. We did not know.

rows.speaker: Dorn
rows.following: Twenty feet south, a newer pipe crossed. Not on map. I looked between them.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: Twenty feet south, a newer pipe crossed. Not on map. I looked between them.

rows.following: The map had not caught up. I wrote less now.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: Dorn said, “Drink.” We ate lunch under a tree. The ground was damp. I sat on my bag. Pessa ate bread and dried fruit. Dorn had eggs again.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: I hated him. Pessa laughed. We ate. I flexed my hand. Fine. No magic yet. No need. My legs were more tired from walking than yesterday. Good tired. Normal. I drank. Pessa looked west.
rows.current: “We can finish the upper loop by midafternoon.”

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.following: Right. Two days. Then done. I had expected something else. Not danger. More. Because stories liked escalation. Roads did not care about narrative. Apparently jobs didn't either. Good. Before the upper loop, I was wrong about a culvert. Not spectacularly. Enough.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: The crossing sat below a pasture where the ditch widened into a shallow green pool. Water stood almost to the culvert mouth. The downstream side ran clear. I looked at the upstream pool.

rows.speaker: Pessa
rows.following: I stopped. Water near an inlet looked like backed water. That was not the same thing. Dorn put the probe into the pool edge. Shallow. Then deeper. The pasture itself dipped toward the road.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.following: “Then don't create work because water looks dramatic.”

rows.speaker: Pessa
rows.current: “Then don't create work because water looks dramatic.”
rows.following: That hurt. Reasonably. I crossed out the note I had started. Dorn said, “You can keep it for your memoir.”

rows.speaker: GREG

rows.current: “I will kill you with your probe.”

rows.following: Pessa laughed. We moved on. The mistake bothered me for perhaps six minutes. Then less. My inference had been reasonable. It had also been wrong because I had treated water level as evidence of restriction without checking the grade that produced the water level. Useful. Not universal. I did not write a principle. This required restraint. Then we finished the upper loop.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: Dorn found a broken iron strap in the ditch and kept it.

rows.speaker: Pessa
rows.following: Strong. On the return, we reached the long downhill wash again. A loaded cart was coming up. Two horses. Barrels. Not huge. Heavy enough. The driver saw us and kept center. Good. Then another cart appeared behind him. Empty. Faster. The road was wide enough to pass in most places. Not beside the washed shoulder. I saw it. Pessa saw it. We were off the road already.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: The empty driver started moving out to pass. I stepped forward. Red paddle? No paddle. Wrong job. I raised both arms.
rows.following: The empty driver slowed. Not stopped.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: I counted accidentally. Seven. Fuck. At the south-west gate, Pessa stopped.
rows.following: We went. The clerk took our packet. Pessa gave the summary. Not me. Red seep. Paired culvert with unrecorded collapsed side and farm fill. Blue shoulder erosion. Routine marks. Temporary loaded-wheel center guidance at two locations until crews assessed. The clerk asked questions. Pessa answered. Dorn added the hidden repair fill. I added one detail when Pessa looked at me. Only one.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: No joke. She noticed that too.

rows.following: Dorn said, “Drinks?” I looked at the light. Third evening bell later.

rows.following: Dorn grinned. We split at the Guild steps. Pessa went toward the road office. Dorn toward the market. I went home. The room was still mine. Another week. I unpacked. Road bag empty. Dirty socks. Food gone except one piece of cheese. Inspection copy folded. I took the calendar down. Crossed out ROAD DAY TWO.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: He was late. Of course. Third evening bell passed. Then another ten minutes. I sat outside the drink shop with a cup I had not started because apparently I had standards now. Jorren arrived first.
